sentences.zh: 柳世隆

translations.literal: Liu Shilong
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shilong

sentences.zh: 柳世隆字彥緒，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shilong, styled Yanxu, was a native of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shilong, styled Yanxu, was a man of Jie in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖憑，馮翊太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ping was Administrator of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ping had been administrator of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 父叔宗，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Shuzong died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuzong died young.

sentences.zh: 世隆少有風器，伯父元景，宋大明中爲尚書令，獨賞愛之，異於諸子。

translations.literal: Shilong from youth had presence and capacity. His paternal uncle Yuanjing, in the Daming era of Song was Director of the Masters of Writing; he alone favored and loved him, treating him differently from his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong showed talent and bearing from youth. His uncle Yuanjing, who under Song had been director of the masters of writing in the Daming era, singled him out for affection above his own sons.

sentences.zh: 言於孝武帝，得召見，帝曰：「三公一人，是將來事也。

translations.literal: He spoke of him to Emperor Xiaowu, and Shilong was summoned to audience. The emperor said: 「Of the Three Dukes there will be one—and that will be a matter for the future.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing spoke of him to Emperor Xiaowu, and Shilong was summoned to court. The emperor said: 「One of the Three Dukes—this boy will be that man in time to come.

sentences.zh: 」海陵王休茂爲雍州，辟世隆爲迎主簿。

translations.literal: 」Prince of Hailing Xiu Mao was in Yong province; he recruited Shilong as welcoming chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: 」When Prince of Hailing Xiu Mao held Yong province, he took Shilong on as welcoming chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 除西陽王撫軍法曹行參軍，出爲虎威將軍、上庸太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting aide in the law bureau on the staff of the Prince of Xiyang's pacification army, then went out as General of Tiger Might and Administrator of Shangyong.
translations.idiomatic: He was named acting aide in the law bureau on Prince of Xiyang's pacification staff, then sent out as general of tiger might and administrator of Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 帝謂元景曰：「卿昔以虎威之號爲隨郡，今復以授世隆，使卿門世不絕公也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yuanjing: 「You once bore the title Tiger Might as Administrator of Sui commandery; now I give it again to Shilong, so that your house may never lack a lord among the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Yuanjing: 「You once held the tiger might title in Sui; I now give it again to Shilong, so your line may never lack a duke.

sentences.zh: 」元景爲景和所殺，世隆以在遠得免。

translations.literal: 」Yuanjing was killed by Jinghe; Shilong, because he was far away, escaped.
translations.idiomatic: 」Yuanjing was put to death in the Jinghe purge; Shilong, posted far away, escaped.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，諸州反叛，世隆以門禍獲申，事由明帝，乃據郡起兵，遣使應朝廷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, when the provinces rebelled, Shilong's family disaster was cleared through Emperor Ming; on that account he raised troops in his commandery and sent envoys to answer the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first years of Taishi, when the provinces rose in revolt, Shilong's clan was cleared of guilt through Emperor Ming; he then seized his commandery, raised arms, and sent envoys to the throne.

sentences.zh: 弘農人劉僧驎亦聚衆應之。

translations.literal: Liu Senglin of Hongnong also gathered a band to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Senglin of Hongnong likewise raised a force in support.

sentences.zh: 收合萬人，奄至襄陽萬山，爲孔道存所破，衆皆奔散，僅以身免，逃藏民閒，事平乃出。

translations.literal: He gathered ten thousand men and suddenly reached Wanshan by Xiangyang, but was broken by Kong Daocun; the host scattered in flight, and he barely escaped with his life, hiding among the people until the affair was settled and only then came forth.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered ten thousand men and struck suddenly at Wanshan outside Xiangyang, but Kong Daocun routed him; the army broke and fled, and he barely escaped alive, living in hiding among common folk until order returned.

sentences.zh: 還爲尚書儀曹郎，明帝嘉其義心，發詔擢爲太子洗馬，出爲寧遠將軍、巴西梓潼太守。

translations.literal: On his return he became Gentleman of Ceremonies in the Masters of Writing; Emperor Ming praised his loyal heart and issued an edict promoting him to Groom of the Heir Apparent, then sent him out as General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of Zitong in Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as gentleman of ceremonies in the masters of writing; Emperor Ming honored his loyalty and promoted him by edict to groom of the heir apparent, then sent him out as general who pacifies the distance and administrator of Zitong in Baxi.

sentences.zh: 還爲越騎校尉，轉建平王鎮北諮議參軍，領南泰山太守，轉司馬、東海太守，入爲通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He returned as Colonel of the Rapid Steeds, transferred to advising staff officer on the pacifying-north staff of Prince of Jianping, with concurrent Administrator of South Taishan, then made marshal and Administrator of Donghai, and entered as attendant cavalier in direct service.
translations.idiomatic: He came back as colonel of the rapid steeds, became advising staff officer on Prince of Jianping's pacifying-north staff while holding South Taishan, then marshal and administrator of Donghai, and entered court as attendant cavalier in direct service.

sentences.zh: 尋爲晉熙王安西司馬，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made chief of staff on the pacifying-west staff of Prince of Jinxi, with the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was chief of staff on Prince of Jinxi's pacifying-west staff, with the additional rank general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 時世祖爲長史，與世隆相遇甚懽。

translations.literal: At that time Shizu was chief of staff, and he and Shilong met with great mutual delight.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu was then chief of staff; he and Shilong took to each other at once.

sentences.zh: 太祖之謀渡廣陵也，令世祖率衆下，同會京邑，世隆與長流蕭景先等戒嚴待期，事不行。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor planned to cross to Guangling, he ordered Shizu to lead troops downstream to meet at the capital; Shilong, with the senior commander Xiao Xianxian and others, stood to arms awaiting the day—but the plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor plotted a crossing at Guangling, he told Shizu to bring the army downriver to the capital; Shilong, with Xiao Xianxian and other senior commanders, stood to arms for the appointed day—but the scheme came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷疑憚沈攸之，密爲之防，府州器械，皆有素蓄。

translations.literal: At that time the court feared Shen Youzhi and secretly made preparations against him; every prefecture and province had long stored arms and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: The court then feared Shen Youzhi and quietly braced against him; arms and gear were stockpiled in every prefecture and province.

sentences.zh: 世祖將下都，劉懷珍白太祖曰：「夏口是兵衝要地，宜得其人。

translations.literal: When Shizu was about to go down to the capital, Liu Huaizhen told the Grand Ancestor: 「Xiakou is a military choke point; it needs the right man.
translations.idiomatic: As Shizu prepared to go to the capital, Liu Huaizhen said to the Grand Ancestor: 「Xiakou is the hinge of the armies; the man there must be the right one.

sentences.zh: 」太祖納之，與世祖書曰：「汝旣入朝，當須文武兼資人與汝意合者，委以後事，世隆其人也。

translations.literal: 」The Grand Ancestor accepted this and wrote to Shizu: 「Once you enter court you will need a man of both civil and martial gifts whose mind matches yours, to entrust with what follows—and that man is Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Grand Ancestor agreed and wrote to Shizu: 「When you come to court you will need someone who unites civil and martial gifts and thinks as you do, to leave affairs in his hands—and that is Shilong.

sentences.zh: 」世祖舉世隆自代。

translations.literal: 」Shizu nominated Shilong to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: 」Shizu put Shilong forward in his own place.

sentences.zh: 轉爲武陵王前軍長史、江夏內史、行郢州事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief of staff on the vanguard staff of Prince of Wuling, Interior Minister of Jiangxia, and acting Inspector of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief of staff on Prince of Wuling's vanguard staff, interior minister of Jiangxia, and acting inspector of Ying.

sentences.zh: 冬，攸之反，遣輔國將軍中兵參軍孫同、寧朔將軍中兵參軍武寶、龍驤將軍騎兵參軍朱君拔、寧朔將軍沈惠眞、龍驤將軍騎兵參軍王道起三萬人爲前驅，又遣司馬冠軍劉攘兵領寧朔將軍外兵參軍公孫方平、龍驤將軍騎兵參軍朱靈眞、沈僧敬、龍驤將軍高茂二萬人次之，又遣輔國將軍王靈秀、丁珍東、寧朔將軍中兵參軍王彌之、寧朔將軍外兵參軍楊景穆二千匹騎分兵出夏口，據魯山。

translations.literal: In winter Youzhi rebelled. He sent Pacifying State General and central corps staff officer Sun Tong, Pacifying North General and central corps staff officer Wu Bao, Flying Dragon General and cavalry corps staff officer Zhu Junba, Pacifying North General Shen Huizhen, and Flying Dragon General and cavalry corps staff officer Wang Daoqi—thirty thousand men as vanguard. He also sent Champion Marshal Liu Rangbing leading Pacifying North General and outer corps staff officer Gongsun Fangping, Flying Dragon General and cavalry corps staff officers Zhu Lingzhen and Shen Sengjing, and Flying Dragon General Gao Mao—twenty thousand as the second echelon. He further sent Pacifying State General Wang Lingxiu, Ding Zhendong, Pacifying North General and central corps staff officer Wang Mizhi, and Pacifying North General and outer corps staff officer Yang Jingmu with two thousand horse to divide forces out from Xiakou and seize Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Youzhi rose in revolt. He sent Sun Tong, pacifying state general and central corps staff officer; Wu Bao, pacifying north general and central corps staff officer; Zhu Junba, flying dragon general and cavalry corps staff officer; Shen Huizhen, pacifying north general; and Wang Daoqi, flying dragon general and cavalry corps staff officer—with thirty thousand men as vanguard. He sent champion marshal Liu Rangbing at the head of Gongsun Fangping, pacifying north general and outer corps staff officer; Zhu Lingzhen and Shen Sengjing, flying dragon generals and cavalry corps staff officers; and Gao Mao, flying dragon general—with twenty thousand in the second wave. He sent pacifying state general Wang Lingxiu, Ding Zhendong, pacifying north general and central corps staff officer Wang Mizhi, and pacifying north general and outer corps staff officer Yang Jingmu with two thousand horse to split from Xiakou and hold Lushan.

sentences.zh: 攸之乘輕舸從數百人先大軍下住白螺洲，坐胡牀以望其軍，有自驕色。

translations.literal: Youzhi took a light boat with several hundred men and went ahead of the main army to moor at White Snail Islet; he sat on a folding camp chair to watch his troops, with a look of self-satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi went ahead in a light boat with a few hundred men, moored at White Snail Islet before the main host, and sat on a camp chair to watch his army—plainly pleased with himself.

sentences.zh: 旣至郢，以郢城弱小不足攻，遣人告世隆曰：「被太后令，當蹔還都。

translations.literal: When he reached Ying he judged the city small and weak and not worth attacking; he sent a man to tell Shilong: 「By the empress dowager's order I am to return to the capital for a time.
translations.idiomatic: At Ying he thought the town too small and weak to bother with; he sent word to Shilong: 「The empress dowager has ordered me to return to the capital for the moment.

sentences.zh: 卿旣相與奉國，想得此意。

translations.literal: You, who serve the state with me, will surely grasp my meaning.
translations.idiomatic: You serve the realm as I do—you will surely take my meaning.

sentences.zh: 」世隆使人答曰：「東下之師，久承聲問。

translations.literal: 」Shilong sent a reply: 「Your army marching east has long been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: 」Shilong answered: 「We have long had word of your host coming east.

sentences.zh: 郢城小鎮，自守而已。

translations.literal: This little town of Ying can only hold itself.
translations.idiomatic: This little fortress of Ying can only defend itself.

sentences.zh: 」攸之將去，世隆遣軍於西渚挑戰，攸之果怒，令諸軍登岸燒郭邑，築長圍攻道，顧謂人曰：「以此攻城，何城不剋！

translations.literal: 」As Youzhi was about to leave, Shilong sent troops to challenge him at the western ford; Youzhi grew angry as expected, ordered his armies ashore to burn the suburbs, built a long encirclement and assault works, and said to those about him: 「With this we take cities—what city would not fall!
translations.idiomatic: 」When Youzhi was ready to go, Shilong provoked a fight at the western crossing; Youzhi flew into a rage, had his men land and burn the outer town, threw up a long siege line, and told his officers: 「With this way of war, what wall will not fall!

sentences.zh: 」晝夜攻戰，世隆隨宜拒應，衆皆披却。

translations.literal: 」Day and night they fought; Shilong met each move as needed, and the assailants were driven back on every side.
translations.idiomatic: 」They attacked day and night; Shilong answered each thrust as the moment required, and the enemy was beaten back again and again.

sentences.zh: 世祖初下，與世隆別，曰：「攸之一旦爲變，焚夏口舟艦沿流而東，則坐守空城，不可制也。

translations.literal: When Shizu first went downstream he parted from Shilong and said: 「If Youzhi should suddenly turn traitor, burn the ships at Xiakou and drift east with the current, you would sit in an empty city and be beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu first marched downstream he took leave of Shilong and said: 「If Youzhi turns rebel at once, burns the fleet at Xiakou, and drifts east on the current, you will sit in an empty city with no hold on him.

sentences.zh: 雖留攻城，不可卒拔。

translations.literal: Even if he stays to besiege you, he cannot take the place at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he stays to besiege you, he cannot storm it in a day.

sentences.zh: 卿爲其內，我爲其外，乃無憂耳。

translations.literal: You hold the inside and I the outside—then there is nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: You inside and I outside—then we need not worry.

sentences.zh: 」至是世祖遣軍主桓敬、陳胤叔、苟元賔等八軍據西塞，令堅壁以待賊疲。

translations.literal: 」Now Shizu sent the army commanders Huan Jing, Chen Yingshu, Gou Yuanbin, and others with eight armies to hold the western passes, ordering them to strengthen their walls and wait until the rebels were worn down.
translations.idiomatic: 」Now Shizu sent Huan Jing, Chen Yingshu, Gou Yuanbin, and other commanders with eight armies to hold the western forts, with orders to stand behind strong walls until the rebels were spent.

sentences.zh: 慮世隆危急，遣腹心胡元直潛使入郢城通援軍消息，內外竝喜。

translations.literal: Fearing Shilong was in peril, he sent his trusted man Hu Yuanzhi in secret into Ying to carry word of the relief armies; inside and outside alike rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid Shilong was hard pressed, he sent his intimate Hu Yuanzhi secretly into Ying with news of the relief force; city and camp alike took heart.

sentences.zh: 尚書符曰：

translations.literal: A dispatch from the Masters of Writing reads:
translations.idiomatic: The ministry dispatch reads:

sentences.zh: :　　沈攸之出自壟畝，寂寥累世。

translations.literal: : Shen Youzhi rose from the fields; for generations his house was obscure.
translations.idiomatic: : Shen Youzhi came up from the plowlands; his line had been obscure for generations.

sentences.zh: 故司空沈公，以從父宗廕，愛之若子，羽翼吹噓，得昇官次。

translations.literal: The late Minister of Works Lord Shen, taking him into the clan shelter of a paternal uncle, loved him as a son; with wings spread and breath behind him, he climbed the ladder of office.
translations.idiomatic: The late minister of works Lord Shen took him in under a kinsman's wing and loved him as a son; favored and pushed forward, he rose rung by rung in office.

sentences.zh: 景和昏悖，猜畏柱臣，而攸之凶忍，趣利樂禍，請銜詔旨，躬行反噬。

translations.literal: Jinghe was benighted and perverse, suspicious of the pillar ministers; Youzhi was fierce and cruel, greedy for profit and glad of disaster—he asked to bear the imperial command and himself turned to bite his benefactor.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghe was mad and cruel, fearful of his great ministers; Youzhi was savage and greedy, eager for gain and glad of ruin—he begged the edict and with his own hand turned on the man who had raised him.

sentences.zh: 又攸之與譚金、童泰壹等暴寵狂朝，竝爲心膂，同功共體，世號「三侯」。

translations.literal: Again, Youzhi with Tan Jin, Tong Taiyi, and others were violently favored in that frantic court; together they were heart and backbone, sharing merit and one body—the age called them the 「Three Marquises.」
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi, Tan Jin, Tong Taiyi, and others had been wildly favored in that deranged court; they were heart and sinew together, one body in merit—the age named them the 「Three Marquises.」

sentences.zh: 當時親昵，情過管、鮑，仰遭革運，凶黨懼戮，攸之反善圖全，用得自免。

translations.literal: In those days their intimacy surpassed Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya; then the revolution came, the wicked feared execution, and Youzhi turned to schemes of self-preservation and so slipped free.
translations.idiomatic: Their bond then outdid Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya; when the throne changed, the guilty feared the axe, and Youzhi turned every trick to save himself and walked away.

sentences.zh: 旣殺從父，又虐良朋，雖呂布販君，酈寄賣友，方之斯人，未足爲酷。

translations.literal: He had already killed a paternal uncle and abused good friends; though Lü Bu sold out his lord and Li Ji betrayed his friend, set beside this man they are not cruel enough.
translations.idiomatic: He killed a kinsman and tormented true friends; Lü Bu who sold his ruler and Li Ji who sold his friend—beside this man they hardly count as cruel.

sentences.zh: 泰始開闢，網漏吞舟，略其凶險，取其搏噬，故階亂獲全，因禍興福。

translations.literal: When Taishi opened the reign, the net let the great fish pass; his ferocity was overlooked and only his bite was taken—so he climbed through chaos unscathed and turned disaster into fortune.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taishi the law forgave the great offender; his violence was passed over and only his teeth were used—so he rose whole from rebellion and made calamity his ladder.

sentences.zh: :　　攸之稟性空淺，躁而無謀，濃湖土崩，本非己力，彭城、下邳，望旗宵遁，再棄王師，久應肆法，值先帝宥其回溪之恥，冀有封崤之捷，故得幸會推遷，頻煩顯授。

translations.literal: : Youzhi's nature is shallow and empty, rash and without plan. At Nonghu the earthworks collapsed—no victory of his own; at Pengcheng and Xiapi he fled at the sight of banners by night, twice abandoning the royal army. Long ago he deserved death by law; the late emperor pardoned the shame of Huixi, hoping for the triumph of Feng and Yao—so by luck he was pushed upward, again and again given high office.
translations.idiomatic: : Youzhi is shallow and rash, without counsel. At Nonghu the ramparts gave way—no strength of his; at Pengcheng and Xiapi he ran at the first banner by night, twice deserting the imperial host. He should have died by statute long since; the late emperor spared the disgrace of Huixi, hoping he might yet win a victory like Feng and Yao—so fortune lifted him, and high posts came again and again.

sentences.zh: 內端戎禁，外綏萬里。

translations.literal: Within he held the inner guard; without he soothed ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Within he held the inner armies; without he quieted the realm for ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 聖去鼎湖，遠頒顧命，託寄崇深，義感金石。

translations.literal: When the sage departed for Lake Ding, he sent his final charge from afar; the trust placed in him was deep, his duty moving as metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage went to Ding Lake, a dying charge reached him from afar; the trust was profound, the bond strong as metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 而攸之始奉國諱，喜形于顏，普天同哀，己以爲慶。

translations.literal: Yet when Youzhi first received the state mourning, joy showed on his face; all under heaven grieved together, but he took it for celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Youzhi first took up the state mourning, joy sat plain on his face; the empire mourned as one, and he made it his feast.

sentences.zh: 累登蕃岳，自郢遷荊。

translations.literal: He rose again and again to great provincial posts, moving from Ying to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed repeatedly to great provincial commands, from Ying to Jing.

sentences.zh: 晉熙王以皇弟代鎮，地尊望重，攸之斷割候迎，肆意陵略。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jinxi, the emperor's younger brother, replaced him in the command, his station was lofty and his weight heavy; Youzhi cut off supplies for his reception and wantonly overrode him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jinxi, the emperor's brother, came to relieve him—rank high, name weighty; Youzhi choked off his welcome, seized what he pleased, and rode over him at will.

sentences.zh: 料擇士馬，簡算器械，權撥精銳，竝取自隨。

translations.literal: He selected troops and horses, inventoried weapons and gear, arbitrarily allocated crack forces, and took them all with him.
translations.idiomatic: He picked over men and horses, tallied arms and gear, stripped the best troops on his own authority, and kept them all for himself.

sentences.zh: 郢城所留，十不遺一。

translations.literal: Of what was left at Ying, not one in ten remained.
translations.idiomatic: What he left in Ying did not amount to one man in ten.

sentences.zh: 專恣鹵奪，罔顧國典。

translations.literal: Monopolizing plunder at will, heedless of state law.
translations.idiomatic: He plundered as he pleased and trampled the laws of the realm.

sentences.zh: 踐荊已來，恒用姦數，旣懷異志，興造無端。

translations.literal: Since entering Jing he constantly used deceit; already he harbored disloyal intent and raised trouble without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Since he took Jing he had lived by trickery; disloyalty was already in his heart, and he stirred up trouble without end.

sentences.zh: 乃蹙迫羣蠻，騷擾山谷，揚聲討伐，盡戶上丁。

translations.literal: Then he drove the tribal peoples, disturbed the valleys, proclaimed campaigns, and registered every household's fighting men.
translations.idiomatic: He harried the hill tribes, roiled the valleys, cried war on every side, and levied every able man from every door.

sentences.zh: 蟻聚郭邑，伺國衰盛，從來積年，求不解甲。

translations.literal: They swarmed walled towns like ants, watching whether the state rose or fell; for years on end they sought never to stand down from arms.
translations.idiomatic: They massed at the walled towns like ants, weighing the realm's strength year by year, and for years on end would not lay arms aside.

sentences.zh: 遂四野百縣，路無男人，耕田載租，皆驅女弱。

translations.literal: Thus in a hundred counties across four fields the roads held no men; plowing fields and hauling rent—all were driven by women and the weak.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred counties across the countryside went without men on the roads; only women and the frail were left to till the fields and haul the tax grain.

sentences.zh: 自古酷虐，未聞於此。

translations.literal: Cruelty such as this has been unheard since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, cruelty like this has never been heard of.

sentences.zh: :　　昔歲桂陽內奰，宗廟阽危。

translations.literal: Last year Guiyang rose in internal rebellion and the ancestral temple teetered on the brink.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Guiyang rebelled from within and the ancestral temple stood on the edge of ruin.

sentences.zh: 攸之任官上流，兵彊地廣，勤王之舉，寔宜悉行。

translations.literal: Youzhi held office on the upper reaches with strong troops and broad lands; the king's rescue ought fully to have been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi held the upper Yang with strong armies and wide territory; the call to save the throne should have been answered in full.

sentences.zh: 裁遣羸弱，不滿三千，至郢州稟受節度，欲令判否之日，委罪晉熙。

translations.literal: He sent only the weak, fewer than three thousand; reaching Ying to receive command, he meant that when judgment fell the blame would be laid on Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent only the feeble, fewer than three thousand men; once at Ying he would take orders so that, when the verdict came, guilt would fall on the Prince of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 招誘劔客，羈絆行侶，竄叛入境，輙加擁護，逋亡出界，必遣窮追。

translations.literal: He enticed swordsmen and bound traveling companions; rebels fleeing in he promptly sheltered, fugitives crossing the border he surely sent in relentless pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited bravos and detained wayfarers; deserters who slipped in he shielded at once, and anyone who fled across the border he hunted to the end.

sentences.zh: 視吏若讎，遇民如草，峻太半之賦，暴參夷之刑，鞭箠國士，全用虜法，一人逃亡，闔宗捕逮。

translations.literal: He treated officials as enemies and the people as grass; he imposed harsh taxes of more than half, inflicted violent punishments of the three extremes, flogged gentlemen of the state, and wholly used barbarian law—if one man fled, the whole clan was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Officials he treated as foes and common folk as weeds; he took more than half in tax, punished with the cruellest laws, flogged men of rank, and ruled wholly by barbarian ways—one fugitive, and the whole clan was dragged in.

sentences.zh: 皇朝赦令，初不遵奉，曠蕩之澤，長隔彼州，人懷怨望，十室而九。

translations.literal: Imperial amnesties he at first did not obey; the broad pardon's grace long stayed cut off from that province; men's hearts held resentment—nine households in ten.
translations.idiomatic: He would not heed the court's amnesties; the throne's mercy never reached his province; resentment ran so deep that nine houses in ten were bitter.

sentences.zh: 今乃舉兵內侮，姦回外熾，斯寔惡熟罪成之辰，決癰潰疽之日。

translations.literal: Now he raises troops to insult the realm within while treachery flares without—truly the hour when evil ripens and guilt is complete, the day to lance the abscess and burst the boil.
translations.idiomatic: Now he turns his arms inward while treason blazes abroad—the hour when his wickedness has ripened and his guilt is full, the day to cut the sore and drain the poison.

sentences.zh: 幕府過荷朝寄，義百常憤，董御元戎，龔行天罰。

translations.literal: The headquarters, overburdened with the court's trust, righteous anger a hundredfold, directs the main army and bears heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: This headquarters, charged beyond measure with the court's trust, burns with righteous wrath; it commands the host and carries out heaven's judgment.

sentences.zh: :　　今遣新除使持節郢州司州之義陽諸軍事平西將軍郢州刺史聞喜縣開國侯黃回、員外散騎常侍輔國將軍驍騎將軍重安縣開國子軍主王敬則、屯騎校尉長壽縣開國男軍主王宜與、屯騎校尉陳承叔、右軍將軍葛陽縣開國男彭文之、驃騎行參軍振武將軍邰宰，精甲二萬，衝其首旆。

translations.literal: Now we send the newly appointed Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Ying, Marquis of Wenxi, Huang Hui; Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Assists the State, General of Valiant Cavalry, Baron of Chong'an, army commander Wang Jingze; Commandant of Valiant Cavalry, Baron of Changshou, army commander Wang Yixing; Commandant of Valiant Cavalry Chen Chenshu; General of the Right Army, Baron of Geyang, Peng Wenzhi; and Adjutant of the Flying Cavalry, General Who Quells Martial Foes, Tai Zai—with twenty thousand picked armor to strike his vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: We now send the newly appointed Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Ying, Marquis of Wenxi, Huang Hui; Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Assists the State and General of Valiant Cavalry, Baron of Chong'an, army commander Wang Jingze; Commandants of Valiant Cavalry Wang Yixing, Baron of Changshou, and Chen Chenshu; General of the Right Army Peng Wenzhi, Baron of Geyang; and Flying-Cavalry adjutant Tai Zai, General Who Quells Martial Foes—with twenty thousand elite troops to break his van.

sentences.zh: 又遣散騎常侍游擊將軍湘南縣開國男呂安國、持節寧朔將軍越州刺史孫曇瓘、屯騎校尉寧朔將軍崔慧景、寧朔將軍左軍將軍新亭侯任候伯、龍驤將軍虎賁中郎將尹略、屯騎尉南城令曹虎頭、輔國將軍驍騎將軍蕭順之、新除寧朔將軍游擊將軍下邳縣開國子垣崇祖等，舳艫二萬，駱驛繼邁。

translations.literal: We also send Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Raiding Attack, Baron of Xiangnan, Lu Anguo; Bearer of the Staff, General of Pacifying the North, Inspector of Yue, Sun Tanxuan; Commandant of Valiant Cavalry, General of Pacifying the North, Cui Huijing; General of Pacifying the North and General of the Left Army, Marquis of Xinting, Ren Houbo; General of the Flying Dragon and Tiger-Gallant Central Commander Yin Lue; Commandant of Valiant Cavalry and magistrate of Nancheng, Cao Hutou; General Who Assists the State and General of Valiant Cavalry Xiao Shunzhi; and the newly appointed General of Pacifying the North, General of Raiding Attack, Baron of Xiapi, Yuan Chongzu and others—with twenty thousand war vessels pressing forward in relays.
translations.idiomatic: We also send Lu Anguo, Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of Raiding Attack, Baron of Xiangnan; Sun Tanxuan, Bearer of the Staff, General of Pacifying the North and Inspector of Yue; Commandants of Valiant Cavalry Cui Huijing and Ren Houbo, Marquis of Xinting; Yin Lue, General of the Flying Dragon; Cao Hutou, Commandant of Valiant Cavalry and magistrate of Nancheng; Xiao Shunzhi, General Who Assists the State and General of Valiant Cavalry; and Yuan Chongzu, newly appointed General of Pacifying the North and General of Raiding Attack, Baron of Xiapi—with twenty thousand warships driving forward without pause.

sentences.zh: 又遣屯騎校尉苟元賔、撫軍參軍郭文考、撫軍中兵參軍程隱雋、奉朝請諸襲光等，輕艓一萬，截其津要。

translations.literal: We also send Commandant of Valiant Cavalry Gou Yuanbin, Staff Officer of the Pacifying Army Guo Wenkao, Central Army Staff Officer of the Pacifying Army Cheng Yinjun, Court Gentleman for the Dynasty Zhu Xiguang, and others—with ten thousand light boats to cut his crossings and key points.
translations.idiomatic: We also send Gou Yuanbin, Commandant of Valiant Cavalry; Guo Wenkao and Cheng Yinjun, staff officers of the Pacifying Army; Zhu Xiguang, Court Gentleman for the Dynasty; and others—with ten thousand light craft to seize his crossings and choke points.

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍周盤龍、後將軍成買、輔國將軍王敕勤、屯騎校尉王洪範等，鐵騎五千，步道繼進，先據陸路，斷其走伏。

translations.literal: General of Valiant Cavalry Zhou Panlong, Rear General Cheng Mai, General Who Assists the State Wang Chiqin, Commandant of Valiant Cavalry Wang Hongfan, and others—with five thousand iron cavalry and foot columns following, first holding the land routes and cutting off his flight and ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Panlong, General of Valiant Cavalry; Cheng Mai, Rear General; Wang Chiqin, General Who Assists the State; Wang Hongfan, Commandant of Valiant Cavalry; and others—with five thousand iron horsemen and infantry columns behind, to seize the roads first and block his escape and ambushes.

sentences.zh: 持節、督雍梁二州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡諸軍事、征虜將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史、襄陽縣開國侯、新除鎮軍將軍張敬兒，志節慷慨，卷甲樊、鄧，水步俱馳，破其巢窟。

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff, Commander of the militaries of Yong and Liang, Jing's Jingling, Sizhou's Suixian, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Commandant Who Pacifies the Man, Inspector of Yong, Marquis of Xiangyang, newly appointed General of the Pacifying Army Zhang Jinger'er—with bold integrity, rolls up armor at Fan and Deng, races by water and land together, and smashes his nest and den.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jinger'er, Bearer of the Staff, commander of Yong and Liang, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Inspector of Yong, Marquis of Xiangyang, newly made General of the Pacifying Army—with fierce loyalty he gathers his armor at Fan and Deng, races by river and road alike, and breaks the rebel's lair.

sentences.zh: 持節、督司州諸軍事、征虜將軍、司州刺史、領義陽太守、范陽縣侯姚道和，義烈梗概，投袂方隅，風馳電掩，襲其輜重。

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff, Commander of the militaries of Sizhou, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Inspector of Si, Administrator of Yiyang, Marquis of Fanyang, Yao Daohe—with righteous fierceness flings his sleeves in the frontier, sweeps like wind and lightning, and raids his baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Daohe, Bearer of the Staff, commander of Sizhou, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Inspector of Si and Administrator of Yiyang, Marquis of Fanyang—with stern honor he springs to the frontier, strikes like storm and lightning, and falls on the rebel's supply train.

sentences.zh: 萬里建旍，四方飛旆，莫不總率衆師，雲翔雷動。

translations.literal: Banners are raised for ten thousand li; pennons fly in the four quarters—none fail to marshal the hosts, cloud-soaring and thunder-shaking.
translations.idiomatic: Standards rise ten thousand li; banners fly from every quarter—every host is mustered, moving like clouds, roaring like thunder.

sentences.zh: 人神同憤，遠邇并心。

translations.literal: Men and spirits share wrath; far and near unite in one heart.
translations.idiomatic: Men and spirits burn with the same wrath; near and far are of one mind.

sentences.zh: :　　今皇上聖明，將相仁愛，約法三章，寬刑緩賦，年登歲阜，家給人足，上有惠民之澤，下無樂亂之心。

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven is sage and bright; generals and ministers are humane and loving; the three clauses of law are in force; punishments are lenient and levies light; years bring full harvests and households have more than enough; above there is grace that benefits the people, below there are no hearts that delight in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The throne is wise and clear; generals and ministers are humane; law is restrained to its essentials, punishments are mild and taxes light; harvests run full and homes are at ease; grace flows from above, and below there is no joy in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 攸之不識天時，妄圖大逆，舉無名之師，驅讎怨之衆，是以朝野審其易取，含識判其成禽。

translations.literal: Youzhi does not know heaven's seasons and vainly plots great treason; he raises an army without name and drives a multitude of those who hate and resent—hence court and countryside judge him easy to take, and those with understanding know he is already a trapped beast.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi cannot read the times and dreams of treason; he marches without just cause and leads men who hate him—so court and country alike see him as easy prey, and every clear eye knows the trap has already closed.

sentences.zh: 彼土士民，罹毒日久，今復相逼迫，投赴鋒刃。

translations.literal: The gentry and people of that land have long suffered poison; now again they are pressed hard and rush to the blade's edge.
translations.idiomatic: The people of that region have borne his poison for years; now they are driven again straight onto the swords.

sentences.zh: 交戰之日，蘭艾難分，去就在機，望思先曉，無使一人迷疑，而九族就禍也。

translations.literal: On the day of battle, orchid and mugwort are hard to separate; stay or go hangs on the moment—may you think first and know early, and let not one man in doubt bring nine clans to disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When blades meet, friend and foe will be hard to tell apart; the choice is yours in an instant—think while there is still time, and do not let one man's hesitation drag nine generations to ruin.

sentences.zh: 弘宥之典，有如皎日。

translations.literal: The charter of great pardon is clear as the bright sun.
translations.idiomatic: Our promise of mercy stands bright as the sun.

sentences.zh: 郢城旣不可攻，而平西將軍黃回軍至西陽，乘三層艦，作羌胡伎，泝流而進。

translations.literal: Ying could not be taken, but Pacifying-West General Huang Hui's army reached Xiyang; riding triple-deck ships and performing Qiang and Hu entertainments, they advanced against the current.
translations.idiomatic: Ying still held, but Huang Hui, General Who Pacifies the West, reached Xiyang with triple-deck warships, Qiang and Hu music playing, rowing upriver against the stream.

sentences.zh: 攸之素失人情，本逼以威力，初發江陵，已有叛者，至是稍多。

translations.literal: Youzhi had long lost men's hearts and originally compelled them by force; when he first left Jiangling there were already deserters, and now there were more still.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi had lost the hearts of his men long before and ruled only by terror; deserters appeared as soon as he left Jiangling, and now they grew by the day.

sentences.zh: 攸之日夕乘馬歷營撫慰，而去者不息。

translations.literal: Youzhi by day and night rode through the camps to comfort them, yet those who left did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night he rode the lines to hearten the troops, yet men kept slipping away.

sentences.zh: 攸之大怒，召諸軍主曰：「我被太后令，建義下都，大事若剋，白紗帽共著耳；

translations.literal: Youzhi was greatly angered and summoned the army commanders, saying: 「I received the Empress Dowager's order to raise righteousness and descend on the capital; if the great affair succeeds, we shall share the white gauze cap together;
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi flew into a rage and called his commanders: 「The Empress Dowager charged me to raise a righteous host and march on the capital. If we win, we shall wear the white gauze cap together;

sentences.zh: 如其不振，朝廷自誅我百口，不關餘人。

translations.literal: if it does not prosper, the court will execute my clan of a hundred mouths—it concerns no others.」
translations.idiomatic: if we fail, the court will kill my household to the last—it has nothing to do with the rest of you.」

sentences.zh: 比軍人叛散，皆卿等不以爲意。

translations.literal: 「Lately soldiers desert and scatter—all because you commanders paid no heed.」
translations.idiomatic: 「Soldiers have been deserting because none of you cared to stop it.」

sentences.zh: 我亦不能問叛身，自今軍中有叛者，軍主任其罪。

translations.literal: 「I also cannot pursue every deserter; from now on, whoever rebels in the army—the commander bears the guilt.」
translations.idiomatic: 「I cannot chase down every runaway; hereafter, any man who deserts—his commander answers for it.」

sentences.zh: 」於是一人叛，遣十人追，竝去不反。

translations.literal: Then, when one man deserted, they sent ten to pursue him; all went and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: After that, one deserter would send ten pursuers after him—and none of the ten came back.

sentences.zh: 莫敢發覺，咸有異計。

translations.literal: None dared report it; all harbored separate plans.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared speak of it; every man nursed his own design.

sentences.zh: 劉攘兵射書與世隆許降，世隆開門納之。

translations.literal: Liu Rangbing shot a letter into the city offering surrender to Shilong; Shilong opened the gate and admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rangbing shot a message over the wall offering surrender; Shilong opened the gate and let him in.

sentences.zh: 攘兵燒營而去，火起乃覺。

translations.literal: Rangbing burned the camp and left; only when fire rose did they realize it.
translations.idiomatic: Rangbing fired the camp and withdrew; the army knew only when the flames climbed.

sentences.zh: 攸之怒，銜鬚咀之。

translations.literal: Youzhi was angry and bit his beard, chewing it.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi raged and chewed at his beard until it tore.

sentences.zh: 收攘兵兄子天賜、女婿張平虜斬之。

translations.literal: He seized Rangbing's nephew Tianci and his son-in-law Zhang Pingfu and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Rangbing's nephew Tianci and his son-in-law Zhang Pingfu and had them beheaded.

sentences.zh: 軍旅大散。

translations.literal: The army scattered in great confusion.
translations.idiomatic: The host broke and fled in chaos.

sentences.zh: 攸之渡魯山岸，猶有數十匹騎自隨。

translations.literal: Youzhi crossed to the shore at Lushan; still only several tens of horsemen followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi forded to the bank at Lushan with only a few dozen riders still at his side.

sentences.zh: 宣令軍中曰：「荊州城中大有錢，可相與還取，以爲資糧。

translations.literal: He proclaimed to the army: 「In Jingzhou city there is much money—we can go back together and take it for provisions.」
translations.idiomatic: He called to the army: 「Jingzhou holds great wealth—come back with me and we will take it for supplies.」

sentences.zh: 」郢城未有追軍，而散軍畏蠻抄，更相聚結，可二万人，隨攸之，將至江陵，乃散。

translations.literal: Ying had not yet sent pursuers, but the scattered soldiers feared Miao raids and gathered again—about twenty thousand—following Youzhi; when they were nearing Jiangling they then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had not yet sent pursuers, but the broken troops, fearing tribal raids, clustered again—some twenty thousand—and trailed Youzhi until, near Jiangling, they melted away.

sentences.zh: 世隆乃遣軍副劉僧驎道追之。

translations.literal: Shilong then sent army aide Liu Senglin in pursuit along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong then sent his deputy Liu Senglin after them on the road.

sentences.zh: 攸之已死，徵爲侍中。

translations.literal: Youzhi was already dead; [Shilong] was summoned as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi was already dead; Shilong was summoned to court as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 仍遷尚書右僕射，封貞陽縣侯，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhenyang with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhenyang with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 出爲左將軍、吳郡太守，加秩中二千石。

translations.literal: He went out as General of the Left and Administrator of Wu commandery, with rank raised to two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General of the Left and Administrator of Wu, with stipend raised to two thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐阼，起爲使持節、都督南豫司二州諸軍事、平南將軍、南豫州刺史，進爵爲公。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor ascended the throne, Shilong was recalled to serve as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of All Military Affairs in Southern Yu and Si provinces, General Who Pacifies the South, and Governor of Southern Yu, and was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Shilong was called back from mourning as Bearer of the Staff, overall commander of Southern Yu and Si, General Who Pacifies the South, and Governor of Southern Yu, and was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 上手詔與司徒褚淵曰：「向見世隆毀瘠過甚，殆欲不可復識，非直使人惻然，實亦世珍國寶也。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a handwritten edict to Minister of Works Chu Yuan, saying, 「When I saw Shilong just now he was wasted by grief beyond measure—almost beyond recognition. It not only moves one to pity; he is truly a treasure of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a handwritten edict to Minister of Works Chu Yuan: 「I have just seen Shilong—grief has wasted him past bearing, nearly past knowing. It is not only pitiful; he is a living treasure of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」淵答曰：「世隆至性純深，哀過乎禮。

translations.literal: 」Yuan replied, 「Shilong's native devotion is pure and deep; his grief exceeds the rites.
translations.idiomatic: 」Yuan answered: 「Shilong's nature is pure and deep, and his mourning goes beyond the rites.

sentences.zh: 事陛下在危盡忠，喪親居憂，杖而後起，立人之本，二理同極，加榮增寵，足以厲俗敦風。」

translations.literal: In serving Your Majesty through danger he was utterly loyal; in mourning his kin he leaned on his staff before rising—both are foundations of being human. In these two he reaches the same height; to add honor and grace is enough to steel custom and deepen the wind.」
translations.idiomatic: In danger he served Your Majesty with full loyalty; in bereavement he leaned on his staff before he could rise—both are the root of humanity, and in both he stands at the limit. To heap honor upon him is to temper custom and thicken the wind of the age.」

sentences.zh: ，進號安南將軍。

translations.literal: , and his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: His title was then advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 是時虜寇壽陽，上敕世隆曰：「歷陽城大，恐不可卒治，正宜斷隔之，深爲保固。

translations.literal: At that time the enemy raided Shouyang. The emperor ordered Shilong, 「Liyang city is large—perhaps it cannot be fortified in haste. It is right to partition and block it off and secure it deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy were then raiding Shouyang. The emperor ordered Shilong: 「Liyang is a great city and may not be made ready in a rush. You should divide and seal it off and hold it in depth.

sentences.zh: 處分百姓，若不將家守城，單身亦難可委信也。

translations.literal: In disposing the people, if they do not bring their families to defend the city, a man alone is hard to trust.」
translations.idiomatic: Set the people in order: if they are not to bring their households to the wall, a lone man is hard to trust with the defense.」

sentences.zh: 」尋又敕曰：「吾更歷陽外城，若有賊至，卽勒百姓守之，故應勝割棄也。」

translations.literal: 」Soon another edict: 「We have reinforced the outer wall of Liyang; if bandits come, immediately compel the people to hold it—so it should be better than abandoning sections.」
translations.idiomatic: 」Soon another edict: 「We are strengthening Liyang's outer works. If raiders come, force the people to hold them at once—that will be better than giving ground piecemeal.」

sentences.zh: 垣崇祖旣破虜，上欲罷併二豫，敕世隆曰：「比思江西蕭索，二豫兩辦爲難。

translations.literal: When Huan Chongzu had already broken the enemy, the emperor wished to abolish and merge the two Yu provinces. He ordered Shilong, 「Lately I consider the region west of the Yangtze depleted; maintaining both Yu provinces is hard.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Chongzu had routed the enemy, the emperor wished to fold the two Yu provinces into one. He told Shilong: 「The lands west of the Yangtze have grown thin; to run both Yu provinces at once is hard.

sentences.zh: 議者多云省一足一，於事爲便。

translations.literal: Discussants mostly say that eliminating one and keeping one would be convenient for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors mostly say that to drop one and keep one would be the practical course.

sentences.zh: 吾謂非乃乖謬。

translations.literal: I consider that not mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: I do not think that wrong.

sentences.zh: 卿以爲云何？

translations.literal: What do you think?
translations.idiomatic: What is your view?

sentences.zh: 可具以聞。

translations.literal: Report in full.」
translations.idiomatic: Lay it out fully for Us.」

sentences.zh: 」尋授後將軍、尚書右僕射，不拜。

translations.literal: 」Soon he was appointed Rear General and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: 」Soon after he was named Rear General and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; he declined the post.

sentences.zh: 世隆性愛涉獵，啓太祖借祕閣書，上給二千卷。

translations.literal: Shilong by nature loved wide reading. He memorialized the Founding Emperor to borrow secret-archive books; the emperor gave him two thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong loved learning and ranged widely in his reading. He asked the Founding Emperor to lend him palace archive books; the throne sent two thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 三年，出爲使持節、督南兖兖徐青冀五州軍事、安北將軍、南兖州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs in Southern Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he went out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of Southern Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 江北畏虜寇，搔動不安。

translations.literal: North of the Yangtze they feared northern raids; the people were restless and uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: North of the river they feared northern raids, and the countryside would not settle.

sentences.zh: 上敕世隆曰：「比有北信，賊猶治兵在彭城，年已垂盡，或當未必送死。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Shilong, 「Lately there is news from the north—the enemy still arrays troops at Pengcheng. Their years are nearly spent; perhaps they will not necessarily come to die.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote Shilong: 「Word from the north says the enemy still drill at Pengcheng. Their years are almost spent; they may not come to throw their lives away.

sentences.zh: 然豺狼不可以理推，爲備或不可懈。

translations.literal: Yet wolves cannot be reasoned with; preparations perhaps cannot slacken.
translations.idiomatic: Yet wolves are not argued into peace—our guard must not slacken.

sentences.zh: 彼郭旣無關要，用宜開除，使去金城三十丈政佳耳。

translations.literal: That outer wall has no strategic importance; it should be cleared away, and thirty zhang from the metal wall would be best.
translations.idiomatic: Their outer rampart is not strategically vital; clear it, and leave thirty paces from the inner wall—that is best.

sentences.zh: 發民治之，無嫌。

translations.literal: Send the people to work on it—no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Set the people to the work; there is no objection.

sentences.zh: 若作三千人食者，已有幾米？

translations.literal: If provisioning for three thousand men, how much grain is already on hand?
translations.idiomatic: If you must feed three thousand men, how much grain is already in store?

sentences.zh: 可指牒付信還。

translations.literal: State it clearly on a memorandum and send it back with the messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Put the figures on a slip and return it with the courier.

sentences.zh: 民閒若有丁多而細口少者，悉令戍，非疑也。

translations.literal: Among the people, wherever there are many able-bodied men and few dependents, order them all to garrison—no scruple.」
translations.idiomatic: Where households have many men of service age and few mouths to feed, garrison them all—without hesitation.」

sentences.zh: 」又敕曰：「昨夜得北使啓，鍾離閒賊已渡淮，旣審送死，便當制加剿撲。

translations.literal: 」Another edict: 「Last night we received a courier's report from the north: between Zhongli the enemy have already crossed the Huai. Since they surely come to die, we should at once organize pursuit and strike.
translations.idiomatic: 」Another edict: 「Last night a northern courier reported that the enemy have crossed the Huai near Zhongli. They mean to fight to the death—organize pursuit and strike at once.

sentences.zh: 卿好參候之，有急令諸小戍還鎮，不可賊至不覺也。

translations.literal: Watch carefully; in emergency order all minor garrisons back to the main posts—do not let them reach you unawares.
translations.idiomatic: Keep close watch. If it turns urgent, pull every minor post back to the main forts—you must not be taken unawares.

sentences.zh: 賊旣過淮，不容邇退散，要應有處送死者，定攻壽陽，吾當遣援軍也。

translations.literal: Once the enemy have crossed the Huai they cannot soon scatter and retreat; there must be a place where men are sent to die—they will surely attack Shouyang. We shall send relief troops.」
translations.idiomatic: Once they are south of the Huai they cannot melt away at once; somewhere they will throw lives into the assault—and Shouyang is the mark. We will send relief.」

sentences.zh: 」又遣軍助世隆，并給軍糧。

translations.literal: 」He also sent troops to assist Shilong and provided army grain.
translations.idiomatic: 」He also sent troops to Shilong's aid and issued army grain.

sentences.zh: 虜退，上欲土斷江北，又敕世隆曰：「呂安國近在西，土斷郢、司二境上雜民，大佳，民殆無驚恐。

translations.literal: When the enemy withdrew, the emperor wished to conduct land registration north of the Yangtze, and again ordered Shilong, 「Lü An'guo lately in the west registered mixed households on the borders of Ying and Si—excellent; the people were hardly frightened.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew, the emperor wished to register native land north of the river and again wrote Shilong: 「Lü An'guo has lately, in the west, registered stray households on the Ying and Si borders—with excellent effect; the people were scarcely alarmed.

sentences.zh: 近又令垣豫州斷其州內，商得崇祖啓事，已行竟，近無云云，殊稱前代舊意。

translations.literal: Lately we also ordered Huan, Governor of Yu, to register within his province; on inquiry Chongzu's memorial showed it already done, with no recent complaints—highly in keeping with former custom.
translations.idiomatic: We have also ordered Huan Chongzu, as Governor of Yu, to do the same within his province; his memorial, when consulted, shows the work finished and no fresh trouble—very much the old policy done right.

sentences.zh: 卿視兖部中可行此事不？

translations.literal: Do you see whether this can be done in the Yan region?
translations.idiomatic: Tell Us whether the same can be carried out in your Yan command.

sentences.zh: 若無所擾，春便就手也。

translations.literal: If it would disturb nothing, begin in spring at once.」
translations.idiomatic: If it will not stir unrest, take it in hand this spring.」

sentences.zh: 」其見親委如此。

translations.literal: 」Such was the trust placed in him.
translations.idiomatic: 」Such was the favor and charge he bore.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, Shilong was made Supernumerary Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu took the throne, Shilong was made Supernumerary Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 世隆善卜，別龜甲，價至一萬。

translations.literal: Shilong was skilled at divination; for special turtle shells he paid up to ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong was skilled at divination; for a choice tortoise carapace he would pay as much as ten thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 永明建號，世隆題州齋壁曰「」。

translations.literal: When the Yongming reign was proclaimed, Shilong wrote on the wall of his prefectural study: 「」.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongming reign title was proclaimed, he inscribed the wall of his prefectural study.

sentences.zh: 謂典籤李黨曰：「我不見也。

translations.literal: He told the registry clerk Li Dang, 「I shall not live to see it.
translations.idiomatic: He told the registry clerk Li Dang, 「I shall not live to see it.

sentences.zh: 」入爲侍中、護軍將軍，遷尚書右僕射，領太子右率，雍州大中正，不拜，改授散騎常侍，尚書左僕射，中正如故。

translations.literal: 」He entered court as Palace Attendant and Defender-General, was moved to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and concurrently served as Right Leader of the Heir Apparent's Guard and Chief Rectifier of Yong Province; he did not accept, and was reassigned Supernumerary Palace Attendant and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, retaining Chief Rectifier as before.
translations.idiomatic: 」He entered court as Palace Attendant and Defender-General, was moved to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and was also named Right Leader of the Heir Apparent's Guard and Chief Rectifier of Yong Province. He declined, and was instead made Supernumerary Palace Attendant and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, with Chief Rectifier unchanged.

sentences.zh: 湘州蠻動，遣世隆以本官總督伐蠻衆軍，仍爲使持節、都督湘州諸軍事、鎮南將軍、湘州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: When the Man of Xiang rose, Shilong was sent with his existing rank to command all armies against the Man; he was then made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of All Military Affairs in Xiang, General Who Guards the South, and Governor of Xiang, retaining Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiang barbarians rose, Shilong was sent in his existing rank to command all armies against them, and was then made Bearer of the Staff, overall commander of Xiang, General Who Guards the South, and Governor of Xiang, with Palace Attendant unchanged.

sentences.zh: 世隆至鎮，以方略討平之。

translations.literal: Shilong reached his post and by strategy pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: At his post he pacified them by strategy.

sentences.zh: 在州立邸治生，爲中丞庾杲之所奏，詔原不問。

translations.literal: In the province he established lodges for profit; the Censor Yü Gao memorialized against him, and an edict pardoned him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he set up lodges for private gain; the Censor Yü Gao impeached him, and an edict pardoned him without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 復入爲尚書左僕射，領衞尉，不拜。

translations.literal: He returned as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrently Minister of the Guard; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and was also named Minister of the Guard; he declined.

sentences.zh: 仍轉尚書令。

translations.literal: He was then moved to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 世隆少立功名，晚專以談義自業。

translations.literal: Shilong in youth built merit and fame; in later years he devoted himself solely to pure talk.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong had built merit and fame in youth; in later years he gave himself wholly to pure talk.

sentences.zh: 善彈琴，世稱柳公雙璅，爲士品第一。

translations.literal: Skilled at the zither, the age called him Lord Liu's Paired Jade and ranked him first among gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He played the zither with mastery; the age called him Lord Liu's twin jades and set him first among cultivated men.

sentences.zh: 常自云馬槊第一，清談第二，彈琴第三。

translations.literal: He often said himself: first with the cavalry lance, second in pure talk, third at the zither.
translations.idiomatic: He used to rank himself: first the cavalry lance, second pure talk, third the zither.

sentences.zh: 在朝不干世務，垂簾鼓琴，風韻清遠，甚獲世譽。

translations.literal: In court he did not meddle in affairs; behind his curtain he played the zither—bearing clear and far, and he won high repute.
translations.idiomatic: In court he would not touch the day's business; behind his curtain he played the zither, clear and remote in bearing, and won the age's praise.

sentences.zh: 以疾遜位，改授侍中，衞將軍，不拜，轉左光祿大夫，侍中如故。

translations.literal: Illness made him yield his post; he was reassigned Palace Attendant and Guardian General; he did not accept, and was moved to Grand Master of the Palace Encampment, retaining Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Illness made him yield his post; he was offered Palace Attendant and Guardian General, declined, and was made Grand Master of the Palace Encampment instead, with Palace Attendant unchanged.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died, at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 詔給東園祕器，朝服一具，衣一襲，錢一十万，布三百匹，蠟三百斤。

translations.literal: An edict granted Eastern Garden secret rites regalia, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, a hundred thousand coins, three hundred bolts of cloth, and three hundred jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him Eastern Garden funeral regalia, a full set of court robes, one suit of garments, a hundred thousand cash, three hundred bolts of cloth, and three hundred jin of wax.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「故侍中左光祿大夫貞陽公世隆，秉德居業，才兼經緯。

translations.literal: Another edict said: 「The late Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Household Grandee, Duke of Zhenyang Shilong, upheld virtue in his station and united talent with statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict read: 「The late Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Household Grandee, Duke of Zhenyang Shilong, bore virtue in his work and joined talent to the warp and woof of rule.

sentences.zh: 少播清徽，長弘美譽。

translations.literal: In youth he spread a clear repute; in maturity he enlarged a fair renown.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he cast a clear name abroad; in his prime he widened a fair renown.

sentences.zh: 入參內禁，出贊西牧，專寄郢郊，剋挫巨猾，超越前勳，功著一代。

translations.literal: Within he served the inner palace; without he aided the western governor; entrusted alone with the approaches to Ying, he crushed a great villain, surpassing earlier merit, his achievement marked for a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Within he served the inner palace; without he aided the western governor; left alone to hold the approaches to Ying, he broke a great villain, outdid former merit, and fixed his fame for a generation.

sentences.zh: 及總任方州，民頌寬德，翼教崇闥，朝稱元正。

translations.literal: When he bore overall charge of a province, the people praised his lenient virtue; at the lofty gates he aided instruction, and the court called him the chief rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: When he held a whole province, the people sang of his gentle rule; at the high gates he helped shape the teaching, and the court hailed him as the court's standard.

sentences.zh: 忠謨嘉猷，簡于朕心，雅志素履，邈不可踰。

translations.literal: Loyal counsels and fine plans were plain to Our heart; his lofty aim and plain conduct were beyond surpassing.
translations.idiomatic: His loyal counsel and fine designs were plain to Our heart; his high purpose and plain walk were beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 將登鉉味，用燮鴻化，奄至薨殞，震慟良深。

translations.literal: He was about to mount to the seasoning of state and harmonize the great transformation, when suddenly he passed—Our shock is very deep.
translations.idiomatic: He was on the verge of tasting the cauldron of state and harmonizing the great transformation, when death came suddenly—Our grief is very deep.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，班劔三十人，鼓吹一部，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with thirty halberd-bearers, one suite of ceremonial music, and Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with thirty halberd-bearers, one suite of ceremonial music, and Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 」上又敕吏部尚書王晏曰：「世隆雖抱疾積歲，志氣未衰，冀醫藥有效，痊差可期。

translations.literal: 」 The emperor again instructed Wang Yan, Minister of Personnel: 「Though Shilong bore illness for years, his spirit had not flagged; We hoped medicine would avail and recovery might be expected.
translations.idiomatic: 」 The emperor again instructed Wang Yan, Minister of Personnel: 「Though Shilong had been ill for years, his spirit had not waned; We hoped the physicians would prevail and recovery was still in sight.

sentences.zh: 不謂一旦便爲異世，痛怛之深，此何可言。

translations.literal: We did not think he would in a single morning pass to another world—the depth of anguish is beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: We never thought that in a single morning he would pass to another world—the depth of pain is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 其昔在郢，誠心夙悃，全保一蕃，勳業克著。

translations.literal: Formerly at Ying he had long shown sincere devotion and wholly preserved the frontier; his merit stood clear.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago at Ying he showed old and earnest loyalty and kept a whole frontier safe; his merit stood clear.

sentences.zh: 尋准契闊，增泣悲咽。

translations.literal: Now, to Our sorrow, We part again, and Our weeping redoubles.
translations.idiomatic: Now, to Our sorrow, We must part again, and Our weeping only deepens.

sentences.zh: 卿同在情，亦當無已已耶！」

translations.literal: You share this feeling—surely your grief has no end either!」
translations.idiomatic: You share this bond—surely your grief knows no end either!」

sentences.zh: 世隆曉數術，於倪塘創墓，與賔客踐履，十往五往，常坐一處。

translations.literal: Shilong was skilled in divination; at Nitang he opened a tomb and walked the site with guests—nine times in ten he would sit in the same spot.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong was versed in number-craft; at Nitang he laid out a tomb and walked the ground with guests—nine visits in ten he would sit in the same place.

sentences.zh: 及卒，墓正取其坐處焉。

translations.literal: When he died, the tomb was placed precisely where he had sat.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the tomb was set exactly where he had sat.

sentences.zh: 著《龜經祕要》二卷行於世。

translations.literal: He authored The Secret Essentials of the Tortoise Classic in two juan, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote The Secret Essentials of the Tortoise Classic in two juan, which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 長子悅，早卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yue died young.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yue died young.

sentences.zh: 張瓌

translations.literal: Zhang Gui
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui

sentences.zh: 張瓌，字祖逸，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui, styled Zuyi, was a man of Wu Commandery, Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, styled Zuyi, came from Wu in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖裕，宋金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu was Song Household Grandee with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu had been Song Household Grandee with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 父永，右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Yong was Right Household Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong was Right Household Grandee.

sentences.zh: 曉音律，宋孝武問永以太極殿前鍾聲嘶，永答「鍾有銅滓」。

translations.literal: He understood music; Emperor Xiaowu of Song asked Yong why the bell before the Hall of Supreme Pole had a hoarse tone, and Yong answered, 「The bell has copper slag.」
translations.idiomatic: Yong understood music; Emperor Xiaowu of Song asked him why the bell before the Hall of Supreme Pole sounded hoarse, and Yong answered, 「The bell still has copper slag in it.」

sentences.zh: 乃扣鍾求其處，鑿而去之，聲遂清越。

translations.literal: He struck the bell to find the spot, chiseled it away, and the tone grew clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: He struck the bell to find the flaw, chiseled it out, and the tone rang clear and bright.

sentences.zh: 瓌解褐江夏王太尉行參軍，署外兵，隨府轉爲太傅五官，爲義恭所遇。

translations.literal: Gui left office as acting staff under the Grand Marshal of Prince Jiangxia, was assigned to outer military affairs, and with the headquarters became a Five Offices aide under the Grand Tutor—favored by Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: Gui first served as acting staff under Prince Jiangxia's Grand Marshal, was assigned to outer military affairs, and when the headquarters shifted became a Five Offices aide under the Grand Tutor, where Yigong favored him.

sentences.zh: 遷太子舍人，中書郎，驃騎從事中郎，司徒右長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Crown Prince Attendant, Secretariat Director, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Fast Cavalry, and Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Crown Prince Attendant, Secretariat Director, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Fast Cavalry, and Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，永拒桂陽賊於白下，潰散，阮佃夫等欲加罪，太祖固申明之，瓌由此感恩自結。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yong had resisted the Guiyang rebels at Baixia and was routed; Ruan Tianfu and others wished to punish him, but the Founding Emperor firmly vouched for him—Gui therefore bonded himself in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yong had held the Guiyang rebels at Baixia and been routed; Ruan Tianfu and others wanted him punished, but the Founding Emperor spoke firmly in his defense—Gui bound himself to the throne in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 轉通直散騎常侍，驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He became Directly Attached Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He became Directly Attached Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪，還吳持服。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father and returned to Wu to wear the garb.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he returned to Wu to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 昇明元年，劉秉有異圖，弟遐爲吳郡，潛相影響。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming, Liu Bing harbored rebellious designs; his younger brother Xia held Wu Commandery and secretly coordinated with him.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 1 Liu Bing nursed treasonous designs; his younger brother Xia held Wu Commandery and secretly moved in step with him.

sentences.zh: 因沈攸之事難，聚衆三千人，治攻具。

translations.literal: Exploiting the crisis of Shen Youzhi, they gathered three thousand men and prepared siege equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Using Shen Youzhi's rebellion as cover, they gathered three thousand men and made siege gear.

sentences.zh: 太祖密遣殿中將軍卞白龍令瓌取遐。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor secretly sent Palace Captain Bian Bailong to order Gui to seize Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor secretly sent Palace Captain Bian Bailong to order Gui to take Xia.

sentences.zh: 諸張世有豪氣，瓌宅中常有父時舊部曲數百。

translations.literal: The Zhang clan had been bold for generations; in Gui's house there were constantly several hundred of his father's old retainers.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhangs had been a bold house for generations; Gui kept several hundred of his father's old retainers in his residence.

sentences.zh: 遐召瓌，瓌偽受旨，與叔恕領兵十八人入郡，與防郡隊主彊弩將軍郭羅雲進中齋取遐，遐踰窗而走，瓌部曲顧憲子手斬之，郡內莫敢動者。

translations.literal: Xia summoned Gui; Gui pretended to accept the order and, with his uncle Shu leading eighteen men, entered the commandery seat; with the defense corps chief, Strong Bow General Guo Luoyun, he advanced into the central hall to take Xia—Xia leaped through the window to flee, and Gui's retainer Gu Xianzi cut him down with his own hand; within the commandery none dared move.
translations.idiomatic: Xia summoned Gui; Gui feigned acceptance and, with his uncle Shu and eighteen men, entered the commandery seat. With Guo Luoyun, chief of the defense corps and a Strong Bow General, he pressed into the central hall to seize Xia. Xia bolted through the window, but Gui's retainer Gu Xianzi struck him down on the spot; in the whole commandery no one stirred.

sentences.zh: 獻捷，太祖以告領軍張沖，沖曰：「瓌以百口一擲，出手得盧矣。

translations.literal: Presenting the victory, the Founding Emperor told the Commandant Zhang Chong, who said, 「Gui staked a hundred lives on one throw—he has drawn the highest lot.
translations.idiomatic: When the victory was reported, the Founding Emperor told Commandant Zhang Chong, who said, 「Gui staked a hundred lives on one cast—and on his first throw drew the winning lot.

sentences.zh: 」卽授輔國將軍、吳郡太守，封瓌義成縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: 」 At once Gui was made General Who Pacifies the State and Administrator of Wu Commandery, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yicheng with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: 」 At once Gui was made General Who Pacifies the State and Administrator of Wu Commandery, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yicheng with a fief of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 太祖故以嘉名錫之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor deliberately bestowed a name of good omen.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor had deliberately granted a name of good omen.

sentences.zh: 除冠軍將軍、東海東莞二郡太守，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Exerts Might and Administrator of the two commanderies Donghai and Dongguan, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was named General Who Exerts Might and Administrator of Donghai and Dongguan, but declined.

sentences.zh: ，增邑二百戶。

translations.literal: , the fief was increased by two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was raised by two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋改封平都。

translations.literal: Soon he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingdu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingdu.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，加領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and additionally put in charge of the Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and also put in charge of the Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷都官尚書，領校尉如故。

translations.literal: In the second year he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat while keeping his commandant post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat while keeping his commandant post.

sentences.zh: 出爲征虜將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 三年，烏程令顧昌玄有罪，瓌坐不糾，免官。

translations.literal: In the third year the magistrate of Wucheng, Gu Changxuan, was guilty of a crime; Gui was punished for failing to investigate and was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Gu Changxuan, magistrate of Wucheng, was guilty of a crime; Gui was faulted for not investigating and was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 明年，爲度支尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he became Director of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Director of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，爲冠軍將軍、鄱陽王北中郎長史、襄陽相、行雍州府州事，隨府轉征虜長史。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor acceded, he was General Who Exerts Might, chief aide to the Prince of Poyang's Northern Army, Administrator of Xiangyang, and acting head of Yongzhou and its headquarters; he shifted with the headquarters to chief aide of the expeditionary force.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, he was General Who Exerts Might, chief aide to the Prince of Poyang's Northern Army, Administrator of Xiangyang, and acting head of Yongzhou and its headquarters; when the headquarters moved he became chief aide of the expeditionary force.

sentences.zh: 四年，仍爲持節、督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡軍事、輔國將軍、雍州刺史，尋領寧蠻校尉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was again made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, the Jingling sector of Yingzhou, and the Suixiang sector of Sizhou, General Who Pacifies the State, and Governor of Yongzhou, and soon also made Commandant Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was again made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, the Jingling sector of Yingzhou, and the Suixiang sector of Sizhou, General Who Pacifies the State, and Governor of Yongzhou, and soon also Commandant Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 還爲左民尚書，領右軍將軍，遷冠軍將軍、大司馬長史。

translations.literal: He returned as Director of the Left Secretariat and also commanded the Right Army; he was promoted to General Who Exerts Might and chief aide to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Director of the Left Secretariat and also commanded the Right Army, then was promoted to General Who Exerts Might and chief aide to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 十年，轉太常。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was made Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 自陳衰疾，願從閑養，明年，轉散騎常侍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He stated his illness and asked to retire for quiet care; the following year he was made Regular Attendant at the Scattered Riders and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and asked to live at ease in retirement; the next year he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 頃之，上欲復用瓌，乃以爲後將軍、南東海太守，秩中二千石，行南徐州府州事，又行河東王國事。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor wished to employ Gui again and made him General of the Rear Guard and Administrator of Southern Donghai, at salary of two thousand dan, acting in Southern Xuzhou headquarters affairs, and also acting for the Prince of Hedong's kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the throne meant to use Gui again and named him General of the Rear Guard and Administrator of Southern Donghai, at two-thousand-dan rank, with acting charge of Southern Xuzhou headquarters and of the Prince of Hedong's kingdom.

sentences.zh: 到官，復稱疾，還爲散騎常侍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On reaching his post he again pleaded illness and returned to serve as Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took office he pleaded illness again and came back as Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendor.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: When Yulin acceded, Gui was given the golden seal and purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: When Yulin took the throne, Gui received the golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: ，給親信二十人。

translations.literal: , twenty confidants were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted twenty personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 鬱林廢，朝臣到宮門參承高宗，瓌託脚疾不下。

translations.literal: When Yulin was deposed, courtiers came to the palace gate to pay respects to Gaozong; Gui pleaded foot ailment and did not go down.
translations.idiomatic: When Yulin was deposed, the court came to the palace gate to attend on Gaozong; Gui claimed a foot ailment and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 海陵立，加右將軍。

translations.literal: When Hailing was enthroned, Gui was made General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing was raised to the throne, Gui was made General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 高宗疑外蕃起兵，以瓌鎮石頭，督衆軍事。

translations.literal: Gaozong feared outer prefectures would rise in arms and placed Gui to garrison Shitou with overall command of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong feared the outer commanderies would rebel and put Gui in Shitou with overall command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 瓌見朝廷多難，遂恒卧疾。

translations.literal: Gui saw troubles mounting at court and hence always lay abed feigning illness.
translations.idiomatic: Gui saw the court drowning in trouble and took to his bed, feigning illness without cease.

sentences.zh: ，轉給事中、光祿大夫，親信如故。

translations.literal: , he was shifted to Supervising Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendor, his confidants unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Supervising Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendor, with his personal attendants as before.

sentences.zh: 月加給錢二萬。

translations.literal: Each month he received an additional grant of twenty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Each month he drew an extra grant of twenty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 二年，虜盛，詔瓌以本官假節督廣陵諸軍事、行南兖州事，虜退乃還。

translations.literal: In year 2 barbarian pressure was heavy; an edict had Gui, in his existing office and with borrowed staff, take overall command of Guangling military affairs and act in Southern Yanzhou; when the barbarians withdrew he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 the northern foe pressed hard; an edict kept Gui in his present rank, lent him the staff of authority, and set him over Guangling armies with acting charge of Southern Yanzhou—he came back when the barbarians withdrew.

sentences.zh: 瓌居室豪富，伎妾盈房，有子十餘人，常云「其中要應有好者」。

translations.literal: Gui's dwelling was lavish; concubines and performers filled his rooms; he had more than ten sons and often said, 「Among them there ought to be some good ones.」
translations.idiomatic: Gui lived in great wealth; singers and concubines packed his halls; he had more than ten sons and would say, 「Surely some of them will turn out well.」

sentences.zh: 建武末，屢啓高宗還吳，見許。

translations.literal: Late in Jianwu he repeatedly memorialized Gaozong to return to Wu and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jianwu he kept asking Gaozong to let him go home to Wu, and at last was allowed.

sentences.zh: 優游自樂，或有譏瓌衰暮畜伎，瓌曰：「我少好音律，老而方解。

translations.literal: He lived at ease and amused himself; some mocked Gui for keeping performers in his old age. Gui said, 「In youth I loved music; only in age do I grasp it.
translations.idiomatic: He took his ease and found his pleasures; some jeered that Gui in his decline still kept performers. Gui said, 「I loved music when I was young and only now, old, begin to understand it.

sentences.zh: 平生嗜欲，無復一存，唯未能遣此處耳。」

translations.literal: Of all my lifelong appetites not one remains—only this I cannot yet put aside.」
translations.idiomatic: Every other taste of my life is gone—only this one I cannot yet send away.」

sentences.zh: 高宗疾甚，防疑大司馬王敬則，以瓌素著幹略，授平東將軍、吳郡太守，以爲之備。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was gravely ill and wary of Grand Marshal Wang Jingze, since Gui was known for practical talent he was given General Who Pacifies the East and Administrator of Wu Commandery as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong lay near death and feared Grand Marshal Wang Jingze, he gave Gui—long famed for practical talent—General Who Pacifies the East and the Wu commandery as a hedge.

sentences.zh: 及敬則反，瓌遣將吏三千人迎拒於松江，聞敬則軍鼓聲，一時散走，瓌棄郡逃民閒。

translations.literal: When Jingze rebelled, Gui sent three thousand officers and clerks to meet him on the Song River; hearing Jingze's battle drums they scattered at once, and Gui abandoned the commandery and hid among the common folk.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingze rose, Gui sent three thousand officers and clerks to hold him on the Song River; at the sound of Jingze's drums they broke and ran, and Gui left the commandery and vanished among the people.

sentences.zh: 事平，瓌復還郡，爲有司所奏，免官削爵。

translations.literal: When things were settled Gui returned to his post; impeached by the authorities, he was removed from office and stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: After the revolt was crushed Gui went back to his post; the authorities impeached him, stripped his office, and took his title.

sentences.zh: 永元初，爲光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Early in Yongyuan he was made Grand Master of Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yongyuan he was again Grand Master of Splendor.

sentences.zh: 尋加前將軍，金章紫綬。
