translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made General of the Van with golden seal and purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made General of the Van, with golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 三年，義師下，東昏假瓌節，戍石頭。

translations.literal: In year 3 the righteous army marched south; Dong Hun lent Gui his staff of authority to garrison Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 the righteous army came south; Dong Hun lent Gui his staff and set him to hold Shitou.

sentences.zh: 義師至新亭，瓌棄城走還宮。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached Xinting, Gui abandoned the city and fled back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army reached Xinting, Gui threw away the fortress and ran back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 梁初復爲光祿。

translations.literal: Early in Liang he was again made Grand Master of Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: At the rise of Liang he was again Grand Master of Splendor.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 【史論】

translations.literal: Historical appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historical appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：文以附衆，武以立威，元帥之才，稱爲國輔。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Culture attaches the multitude; military force establishes awe—a marshal's talent is called a pillar of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Letters win the crowd, arms set the awe—a field commander's gift is what men call a pillar of the realm.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之十年治兵，白首舉事，荊楚上流，方江東下。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi trained troops ten years and took up arms in white hair; Jing-Chu on the upper stream, just as Jiangdong lay downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi drilled armies ten years and rose in arms with white hair; Jing and Chu held the upper stream while Jiangdong lay below.

sentences.zh: 斯驅除之巨難，帝王之大敵。

translations.literal: This was the great hardship of driving out foes, the sovereign's mighty enemy.
translations.idiomatic: That was the great labor of expulsion, an emperor's chief foe.

sentences.zh: 柳世隆勢居中夏，年淺位輕，首抗全師，孤城挑攻，臨埤授策，曾無汗馬，勍寇乖沮，力屈於高墉，亂轍爭先，降奔郢路，陸遜之破玄德，不是過也。

translations.literal: Liu Shilong stood in the heart of the realm, young in years and light in rank; he first met the full host, challenged attack from a lone city, handed down plans from the rampart, and never needed a sweating horse—the fierce foe was thwarted and broke on the high walls; broken ranks raced to be first, surrender fled along the road to Ying—Lu Xun's defeat of Liu Bei was no greater.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shilong held the middle kingdom, young in years and slight in rank; he met the whole army first, dared attack from a lone city, gave strategy from the wall, and never needed a horse to sweat—the fierce enemy faltered and bent on the high ramparts; broken wheels fought to lead, surrender poured down the road to Ying—nothing Lu Xun did to Liu Bei surpassed it.

sentences.zh: 及世道清寧，出牧內佐，體之以風素，居之以雅德，固興家之盛美也。

translations.literal: When the age was settled he went out as governor and served within, with wind-like simplicity and elegant virtue—truly the family's glory.
translations.idiomatic: When the world grew calm he governed abroad and aided within, clothed in plain style and seated in gentle virtue—a house's true splendor.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：忠武匡贊，實號兼資。

translations.literal: In praise: Loyal and martial, he aided and upheld; his title truly said he combined both.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Loyal and martial, he steadied the throne; his posthumous name said he held both gifts.

sentences.zh: 廟堂析理，高壘搴旗。

translations.literal: At court he unraveled principles; at high ramparts he plucked banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the hall he parsed right and wrong; on high walls he tore down flags.

sentences.zh: 游藝善術，安絃拂龜。

translations.literal: In roaming arts he mastered techniques; he set strings aright and brushed the tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: He roamed the arts and knew their craft; he tuned strings and swept the divining shell.

sentences.zh: 義成祚土，功立帝基。

translations.literal: Yicheng blessed the soil of his fief; merit set the emperor's foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng graced his fief's land; his merit laid the emperor's base.
